item.text:
**7B.3 Research Note**

Bottom line: mostly no. I found some real but narrow signs of technocratic or diplomatic separation, especially in procurement and nuclear safety, but the broader 2024 record points to party-state fusion, politicized enforcement, and major-public-contract vulnerability to patronage.

**Positive evidence**
- **e-GP was mandatory for government agencies** | **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority** | **March 6, 2024** | [link](https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html) | BPPA said online procurement was mandatory for agencies and improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. This is one of the clearest signs of a more rules-based procurement process rather than pure discretionary favoritism. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Advancing healthcare excellence: WHO's role in developing the first national medical education strategy in Bangladesh** | **WHO Bangladesh** | **March 4, 2024** | [link](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh) | The health ministry and WHO used workforce studies and a technical working group to build a medical-education strategy. That is direct evidence of evidence-based rule-setting in a public system, though narrow. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Bangladesh completes 2nd JEE using the eJEE platform** | **WHO** | **July 11, 2024** | [link](https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn) | WHO described a peer-reviewed evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This is a real institutional correction signal, but it is sector-specific. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to nuclear non-proliferation, peaceful use** | **Dhaka Tribune** | **April 30, 2024** | [link](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear-non-proliferation-peaceful-use) | Officials said Bangladesh would keep transparency, safety, and IAEA-backed safeguards for nuclear plants. That is a real if narrow example of a high-risk domain being handled as a regulated state function rather than a personal vehicle. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 1B.8, 6B.9
- **Hasina reiterates call for China to help repatriate Rohingyas through Myanmar talks** | **TBS News / UNB** | **July 10, 2024** | [link](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar-895921) | This is the clearest 2024 foreign-policy example I found of using diplomacy and regional mediation rather than force. It shows some separation between state policy and narrow personal political theater. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 1B.8, 6B.8, 6B.10

**Negative evidence**
- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House said the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of opponents and critical media, that corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement was politicized, and that ruling-party control over state resources created coercive economic power. This is strong evidence of state-business-party fusion rather than a clean firewall. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 6B.9, 6B.10
- **Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House said the ruling party manipulated the online information environment, blocked major news sites, and throttled internet and communications around BNP rallies and later unrest. That is direct evidence against separating state power from political control. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 7B.2, 6B.9
- **Little election fizz in Bangladesh as prime minister set for another term** | **Reuters** | **January 4, 2024** | [link](https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/) | Reuters reported the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. That is direct evidence against separating state authority from personal political survival. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | **Reuters** | **July 22, 2024** | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina blamed opponents for deadly violence and kept the curfew in place. This reads as using law enforcement for regime defense rather than keeping state coercion separate from personal survival. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 7B.2, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** | **Reuters** | **July 20, 2024** | [link](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | Reuters described curfew, army deployment, and internet/text shutdowns during the protests. This is strong evidence that coercive state capacity was being used against a political challenge, not insulated from it. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 7B.2, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business** | **Reuters** | **July 26, 2024** | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448) | The internet blackout cut off citizens and business activity during the crisis. That is strong evidence of suppressing scrutiny and using state control to protect power. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 7B.1, 7B.2
- **Billions at Stake: Unveiling the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant's Spiraling Costs and Corruption** | **Bangla Outlook** | **April 23, 2024** | [link](https://en.banglaoutlook.org/news/1099) | The piece alleges major cost inflation and politically linked ancillary contracts around Rooppur. Even if treated cautiously, it points toward public contracts being vulnerable to patronage rather than neutral allocation. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 6B.9, 6B.10
- **AL govt created lawless economy** | **The Daily Star** | **October 31, 2024** | [link](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796) | A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. This is broad, direct evidence against clean separation from business interests. | **QIDs:** 7B.3; also 6B.9, 6B.10

**Synthesis**
- The strongest positive material is sector-specific: procurement formalization, health-sector technical work, nuclear safeguards, and Rohingya diplomacy.
- The stronger negative material is systemic: politicized institutions, state-resource coercion, election manipulation, shutdowns, and corruption/capture claims.
- Taken together, 2024 looks like partial technocratic islands inside a largely fused party-state system, not a consistent firewall between Hasina’s personal/political interests and state decisions.

**Search gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 reporting that directly ties Sheikh Hasina herself or her immediate family to a named state contract, license award, or foreign-policy decision through a documented ownership trail.
- The evidence is mostly indirect but still substantial: systemic patronage, politicized procurement, and coercive use of state power.
